name: Israel in the days of the Judges
charge: Serving Baalim and Ashtaroth; intermarrying with the Canaanites; every man doing right in his own eyes
summary: After Joshua's generation died a generation arose that knew not the Lord. They forsook him for the gods of the peoples round about, took their daughters as wives, and were sold into the hands of Mesopotamia, Moab, Canaan, Midian, Ammon, and the Philistines in turn.
offense: Israel's fall began with a command they had heard, not a law they had never received. They were to overthrow the altars of the inhabitants and make no covenant with their gods. Instead, they left the altars standing, made leagues, and settled among the very snares against which they had been warned (Judges 2:1-3). When they became strong, they put the inhabitants to tribute rather than finish what had been commanded (Judges 1:27-35). Profit did not make that substitution obedience. The marriages followed the settlement, and the worship followed the marriages: they took their daughters, gave their own daughters, and served their gods (Judges 3:5-7). Deuteronomy 7:3-4 had already joined those things together, warning that the son would be turned from following the Lord. Exodus 23:32-33 called the gods of the land a snare. What Israel accepted into its households became what Israel bowed before. They could not preserve the covenant by keeping the land while adopting the worship of its inhabitants. Joshua's generation had seen the works of the Lord, but the generation after them knew neither him nor those works (Judges 2:7-10). The departure was also from instruction: they would not hearken to their judges and returned to their own stubborn way (Judges 2:17-19). Proverbs 3:5-6 commands trust in the Lord instead of leaning on one's own understanding. Every man doing right in his own eyes was not liberty from judgment; it was the abandonment of the rule by which Israel was to live.
judgment: The Lord delivered them to spoilers and sold them into the hands of their enemies. Wherever they went, his hand was against them, as he had sworn (Judges 2:14-15). The nations did not suddenly become greater than the God who brought Israel out of Egypt. Israel had departed from him, and the covenant's curses followed them into the inheritance. The land itself did not shelter a disobedient people. Yet the Lord heard their groaning and raised up judges to deliver them. His mercy was shown repeatedly, but the rest was repeatedly misused: when the judge died, they corrupted themselves more than their fathers (Judges 2:18-19). Nehemiah 9:26-28 rehearses the same history—disobedience, enemies, a cry from trouble, saviours, rest, and another return to evil. Mercy gave opportunity to return; it was not permission to resume the sin. In the days before Jephthah, the Lord told them to cry to the gods they had chosen. Israel then confessed, put away the strange gods, and served him (Judges 10:10-16). Repentance had to reach what they kept and what they did. Hosea 5:15 joins affliction to acknowledging the offense and seeking his face. The nations left among Israel proved whether they would hearken to the commandments: the answer was to be given in obedience, not in tears alone (Judges 2:20-23; 3:1-4).

verses.text: And also all that generation were gathered unto their fathers: and there arose another generation after them, which knew not the Lord, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel.
And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served Baalim:

And they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, which brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods, of the gods of the people that were round about them, and bowed themselves unto them, and provoked the Lord to anger.
And they forsook the Lord, and served Baal and Ashtaroth.

And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies.
Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn unto them: and they were greatly distressed.
Nevertheless the Lord raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them.

And yet they would not hearken unto their judges, but they went a whoring after other gods, and bowed themselves unto them: they turned quickly out of the way which their fathers walked in, obeying the commandments of the Lord; but they did not so.

And when the Lord raised them up judges, then the Lord was with the judge, and delivered them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge: for it repented the Lord because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them.

And it came to pass, when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.
And the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, Hittites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Hivites, and Jebusites:
And they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods.
And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgat the Lord their God, and served Baalim and the groves.
Therefore the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Chushan–rishathaim king of Mesopotamia: and the children of Israel served Chushan–rishathaim eight years.
In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them:
But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.
And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them.
Yea, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils,
And shed innocent blood, even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan: and the land was polluted with blood.
Thus were they defiled with their own works, and went a whoring with their own inventions.
Therefore was the wrath of the Lord kindled against his people, insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance.
And he gave them into the hand of the heathen; and they that hated them ruled over them.
Their enemies also oppressed them, and they were brought into subjection under their hand.
Many times did he deliver them; but they provoked him with their counsel, and were brought low for their iniquity.

Nevertheless they were disobedient, and rebelled against thee, and cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee, and they wrought great provocations.

Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them: and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven; and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.

But after they had rest, they did evil again before thee: therefore leftest thou them in the hand of their enemies, so that they had the dominion over them: yet when they returned, and cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven; and many times didst thou deliver them according to thy mercies;
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.

entries.commentary: An angel of the Most High comes up from Gilgal to Bochim and rehearses the covenant: I made you to go up out of Egypt, I brought you unto the land I sware unto your fathers, and I said I will never break my covenant with you. The command was plain: ye shall make no league with the inhabitants of this land, ye shall throw down their altars. But ye have not obeyed my voice. Why have ye done this? The same is true today in the places where we are scattered: we have made leagues with the inhabitants of the land. We find ourselves in their sports leagues and bowling leagues, at their dinner parties, when the scripture says envy not the oppressor and choose none of his ways. The Most High warned against letting them dwell in the land because they would make us sin against him. Dwelling among them breeds curiosity after their gods: how did these nations serve their gods, what is that thing they are doing with that tree, what are they hanging on the tree, why are they giving each other gifts? That curiosity is the snare, and we are not to add to his commandments or take away from them. Throwing down their altars meant burning their graven images with fire, not even desiring the silver or gold on them, lest it become a snare. The Most High keeps reiterating that we will be snared and trapped by serving what these nations serve. Because Israel disobeyed, the sentence falls: I will not drive them out from before you, but they shall be as thorns in your sides, and their gods shall be a snare unto you. The people lifted up their voice and wept, called the place Bochim, and sacrificed there unto the Most High.

The people served the Most High all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great works he did for Israel. Joshua the son of Nun dies at a hundred and ten years old and is buried in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-heres, in the mount of Ephraim, because Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim; he was buried in the land of his own tribe's inheritance.

That whole generation is gathered unto their fathers, and there arises another generation which knew not the Most High, nor the works he had done for Israel, and the children of Israel do evil and serve Baalim and Ashtaroth. Here a pattern starts to develop: when there is a judge in Israel and he dies, the people just go off. It shows we are a people that need leadership; that is why we are told to trust in the Most High and lean not to our own understanding, and he shall direct our paths. We see the same today. Brothers and sisters come with theories they think are their own thoughts, but those thoughts were given to them, mostly by the television. You are either going to follow the one true living God of Israel or the prince of the power of the air, Satan the devil.

Because Israel forsook the Most High, his anger was hot against them; he delivered them into the hands of spoilers and sold them into the hands of their enemies, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies. Look at us today: Black Lives Matter, hands up don't shoot. We cannot stand before our enemies, so now we beg our enemies to see us as people, to see us as human. Our offence is leaving off the commandments to serve other gods, and the Most High has gone and returned to his place until we acknowledge that offence; in our affliction we will seek him early. Judges is the record of that affliction beginning to come upon our people for turning our backs on the one true living God. Whithersoever they went, the hand of the Most High was against them for evil, and they were greatly distressed. Is that not true today? We wonder why we cannot get anywhere as a people; we have individual millionaires, yet no infrastructure, no farms enough to set up our own stores and feed ourselves, no distribution, no hospitals, no textiles, none of the things a nation needs to sustain a nation. The curse was to be cursed coming in and cursed going out, coming in from war and going out to war, and the same is happening to this very day. Our people do not think we are at war, but when the enemy gives you a false image, a false religion and a false education, slums and ghettos to live in, and bad foods, he is at war with you.

Nevertheless the Most High raised up judges which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them, and yet they would not hearken unto their judges, but went a whoring after other gods and turned quickly out of the way their fathers walked in. It repented the Most High because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them. It was the same in Egypt: he said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people, I have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters, I know their sorrows. We are the apple of his eye; he that toucheth Israel toucheth the apple of his eye. The Most High does not want to see us on the bottom, but we trespassed against his commandments, so we have to be punished for it. When the judge was dead, they returned and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, ceasing not from their own doings nor from their stubborn way. As soon as we got out of the condition we were in, we went right back to doing the same thing again, because this is a rebellious and stubborn people, even to this very day.

Because this people transgressed the covenant and did not hearken, the Most High declares he will not henceforth drive out any of the nations which Joshua left when he died. This is exactly what Joshua warned before he died: if ye cleave unto the remnant of these nations and make marriages with them, know for a certainty the Most High will no more drive them out, but they shall be snares and traps, scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off the good land. In the course of making leagues with the inhabitants, what else did we do? We made marriages with them, the very thing the warning named. The nations were left without being driven out hastily, that through them the Most High might prove Israel, whether they would keep his way to walk therein as their fathers did, or not.

These are the nations the Most High left to prove Israel, even as many as had not known all the wars of Canaan, so that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war: five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites of mount Lebanon. Who are all the Canaanites? [Genesis 10](/bible/genesis/10) lists the families: Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth, and the Jebusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite, the Arvadite, the Zemarite, and the Hamathite, and afterward the families of the Canaanites were spread abroad. They were left to prove Israel, to know whether Israel would hearken unto the commandments of the Most High, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.

The children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. Stop: are those not the same people the Most High said to utterly destroy? But we are dwelling among them. They took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods. The law had said it plainly: thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them, neither shalt thou make marriages with them, for they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods. The law of war made a different stipulation for these people. For far off cities Israel was to proclaim peace first, and if they answered peace they became tributaries, just as we read the tribes putting the Canaanites to tribute. But of the cities of these people, the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth, total destruction, that they teach you not to do after all their abominations which they have done unto their gods. Going out to battle against horses and chariots and people more than thou, Israel was told, be not afraid of them, for the Most High is with thee. He constantly repeats these things because he knew we were going to be a stubborn and rebellious people, and he wants us to acknowledge him and only him. Instead Israel did evil, forgat the Most High, and served Baalim and the groves.

The anger of the Most High was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia, and Israel served him eight years. When they cried unto the Most High, he raised up a deliverer, Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother. The spirit of the Most High came upon Othniel, and he judged Israel. But today our people say, you can't judge me. He judged Israel and went out to war, because the Lord is a man of war. That answers those who ask, when we are out on the streets teaching, where are your women. They are not at war; the Lord is a man of war. And for those who do not think we are at war now: though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh. It is a spiritual war, but we are still nonetheless at war, and the weapon of our warfare today is this Bible, mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds, exposing all the lies on the earth. The Most High delivered Chushan-rishathaim into Othniel's hand, and the land had rest forty years, until Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

The children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Most High, and he strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel because they had done evil. Wait a minute: it says the Most High strengthened him. In Joshua, the hearts of the peoples melted because they heard of the things the Most High did for us; now he is strengthening them against us for breaking his commandments. Eglon gathers the children of Ammon and Amalek, smites Israel, and possesses the city of palm trees, and the children of Israel serve Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.

When the children of Israel cried unto the Most High, he raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded. Notice how the Most High raised up judges of different tribes also: Othniel of Judah, now Ehud of Benjamin. Ehud makes a two edged dagger of a cubit length, girds it under his raiment on his right thigh, and brings the present to Eglon king of Moab, who was a very fat man. Saying, I have a secret errand unto thee, O king, Ehud gets Eglon alone in his summer parlour, tells him, I have a message from God unto thee, and thrusts the dagger into his belly with his left hand, and the fat closes upon the blade so he cannot draw it out. Ehud goes forth and locks the doors of the parlour.

When the servants find the parlour doors locked, they say, surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber; they wait outside because they think he is in there relieving himself, and they tarry till they are ashamed, then take a key and find their lord fallen down dead. Ehud escapes to Seirath, blows a trumpet in the mountain of Ephraim, and leads the children of Israel down, saying, follow after me, for the Lord hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand. They slay of Moab about ten thousand men, all lusty men of valour, and not a man escapes. So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest fourscore years.
After Ehud was Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad; and he also delivered Israel.

A man of mount Ephraim named Micah stole eleven hundred shekels of silver from his own mother, and when he heard her cursing about the missing silver he confessed, I took it, and restored it to her. Instead of rebuking her son, his mother said blessed be thou of the LORD, and told him she had wholly dedicated the silver for him to make a graven image and a molten image. She refused to keep what he returned, took two hundred shekels to the founder, and had idols made to set up in her son's house. A mother buying her son idols was nothing new in Israel; there were mothers who steered a son down the wrong path.
Micah had a whole house of gods. He made an ephod and teraphim and consecrated one of his own sons to be his priest, a counterfeit priesthood serving counterfeit gods.

This verse is the key to understanding the whole book of Judges. With no king and no government, Israel was sheep without a shepherd, and when you see how the people carry on in these chapters, that is why: every man did that which was right in his own eyes. The same individual spirit is around today in those who say join no camp and let no man teach you. Every time the scripture shows Israel without a leadership structure, all manner of wickedness follows, primarily idolatry.

A young Levite of Bethlehemjudah departed to sojourn wherever he could find a place and came to mount Ephraim to the house of Micah. When Micah learned the man was a Levite, of the tribe known for the priesthood and the knowledge of the sacrifices, he offered him a deal: dwell with me, be unto me a father and a priest, ten shekels of silver by the year, a suit of apparel, and thy victuals. He hired himself a personal priest for his idols.

The Levite was content to dwell with him and became as one of his sons. Nothing says the Levite was already in idolatry, but when money was offered he went right along with it; being corrupted for reward was always the Levites' weakness. Then Micah said, now know I that the LORD will do me good, seeing I have a Levite to my priest. A house full of idols and a hired priest over them, yet he expected the Most High to bless him because a Levite was on the payroll. That is how sick in the mind Israel was without leadership.

The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpeh that not one of them would give his daughter unto Benjamin to wife. This follows the previous chapter, where the tribes went to war against Benjamin. The people came to the house of God and sat there till evening before God, lifted up their voices and wept sore, asking why it had come to pass that there should be one tribe lacking in Israel. The next day they rose early, built an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. The children of Israel repented them for Benjamin their brother, for there was one tribe cut off from Israel that day. They had also made a great oath that whoever came not up to the Lord at Mizpeh would surely be put to death.

The question of the chapter: how shall we do for wives for them that remain, seeing we have sworn by the Lord not to give them our daughters? They made a vow, they swore to the Lord, and the law says a sworn oath must be performed; that is why they could not simply turn around and give their daughters.

They searched which tribe came not up to Mizpeh, and behold, none had come from Jabeshgilead to the assembly. So under the great oath the congregation sent twelve thousand of the valiantest men to smite Jabeshgilead with the edge of the sword, destroying every male and every woman that had lain by man. Among the inhabitants of Jabeshgilead they found four hundred young virgins that had not known man by lying with any male, and brought them to the camp at Shiloh in the land of Canaan. Verse 12 is the precept for what it means in scripture to know somebody: to lie with them, meaning to have sex with them.

The whole congregation sent to speak peaceably to the children of Benjamin at the rock Rimmon, and Benjamin came again. They gave them the wives saved alive of the women of Jabeshgilead, but they sufficed not; there were not enough for all the men that remained. The people repented them for Benjamin because the Lord had made a breach in the tribes of Israel, and the elders said there must be an inheritance for them that be escaped of Benjamin, that a tribe be not destroyed out of Israel. Verse 18 restates why they could not just give their own daughters: the children of Israel had sworn, saying, Cursed be he that giveth a wife to Benjamin. That is the same oath read in verse 7.

The solution: there was a yearly feast of the Lord in Shiloh, so they commanded the children of Benjamin to lie in wait in the vineyards, and when the daughters of Shiloh came out to dance in the dances, every man was to catch him a wife of the daughters of Shiloh and go to the land of Benjamin. When the fathers or brethren came to complain, the elders would answer, Be favourable unto them for our sakes; because the fathers did not give their daughters, they would not be guilty of breaking the oath. The children of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number of them that danced, then returned to their inheritance, repaired the cities, and dwelt in them.

The children of Israel departed thence at that time, every man to his tribe, to his family, and to his inheritance. In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes. We see that same thing today: most of our people are still in that state, doing what is right in their own eyes. There is nothing new under the sun. --- Topics: [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high)

Give thanks unto the Most High, for He is good and His mercy endures forever; who can show forth all His praise. Blessed are they that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times. At all times, not only when convenient. David asks to be remembered with the favor toward His people, to see the good of His chosen and rejoice in the gladness of His nation.

We have sinned with our fathers and done wickedly; our fathers understood not His wonders in Egypt and provoked Him at the Red Sea. Nevertheless He saved them for His name's sake, rebuked the Red Sea so it dried up, and led them through the depths as through the wilderness. Esau's science says a wind blew it into a tsunami, but the Most High said He rebuked it. The waters covered their enemies, and then they believed His words and sang His praise.

They soon forgot His works and waited not for His counsel, but lusted exceedingly in the wilderness and tempted God, so He sent leanness into their soul. They envied Moses and Aaron the saint of the Lord; the earth swallowed Dathan and the company of Abiram for their insurrection. They made a calf and worshipped the molten image, changing their glory into the likeness of an ox that eats grass, forgetting God their savior. He would have destroyed them had not Moses stood in the breach. -

They despised the pleasant land and believed not His word but brought up a false report and murmured in their tents; therefore He lifted His hand to overthrow them and scatter their seed among the nations. They joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate the sacrifices of the dead, provoking Him to anger, and the plague broke in upon them. Then Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed; it was counted to him for righteousness unto all generations, for he had zeal in the fear of the Most High. -

They angered Him at the waters of strife, so it went ill with Moses, who spoke unadvisedly with his lips. Moses lost the promised land because he smote the rock and called the people rebels instead of speaking to it and sanctifying the Most High. They did not destroy the nations as commanded but were mingled among the heathen and learned their works. They served idols, sacrificed their sons and daughters to devils, and shed innocent blood, polluting the land and going a-whoring with their own inventions. -

The wrath of the Most High was kindled against His people so that He abhorred His own inheritance and gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them. The heathen ruling in our communities today, the legal system and the government, is the law and the prophets agreeing; He delivered them many times, but they provoked Him and were brought low for their iniquity. Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting. -

On the twenty and fourth day the children of Israel assemble with fasting, sackcloth, and earth upon them, and the seed of Israel separate themselves from all strangers, standing to confess their sins and the iniquities of their fathers. They read in the book of the law a fourth part of the day and another fourth part they confess and worship the Most High, keeping the separation the law required.

The Levites stand up and cry with a loud voice, blessing the glorious name of the Most High who is exalted above all blessing and praise. They confess that the Most High alone made heaven, the earth, the seas, and all that is in them, and the host of heaven worships Him.

The Levites recount how the Most High chose Abram, brought him out of Ur, made covenant with him, saw the affliction in Egypt, divided the sea, and led Israel by the pillar of cloud and fire. He came down upon mount Sinai and spake from heaven, giving right judgments, true laws, good statutes, and commandments, and made known the holy sabbath. Moses was not on the mount only for the ten commandments but received the statutes, the laws, and the precepts, and was so in tune with the Most High that he knew what Jacob prophesied over his sons in the last days. -

The Levites confess that the fathers dealt proudly, hardened their necks, and made a molten calf, saying, This is thy god that brought thee up out of Egypt, working great provocations. Yet the Most High in His manifold mercies forsook them not in the wilderness, the pillar of cloud and fire departing not, giving His good spirit, manna, and water, so that they lacked nothing forty years.

The Most High gives them kingdoms, multiplies their children, and brings them into the land, but the people are disobedient, rebel, cast the law behind their backs, and slay the prophets that testified against them. When they cried in their trouble He heard them from heaven and delivered them many times according to His mercies, yet He did not utterly consume them, for He is a gracious and merciful God. This same stiff-necked resisting is what Stephen charged the fathers with in Acts. -

The Levites appeal to the Most High as the great, mighty, and terrible God who keeps covenant and mercy, confessing that all that came upon them was just, for He did right and they did wickedly. They are servants in the land the Most High gave their fathers, its increase going to the kings set over them for their sins, so they make a sure covenant, write it, and their princes, Levites, and priests seal unto it.

The seven nations cast out before Israel, the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, greater and mightier than Israel, are Hamitic nations. Thou shalt smite them and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them. Since the days of old the Most High has never been about the love-of-the-world gospel; throw that doctrine in the trash. This is why they do not want you reading the old covenant: verses like this correct the miseducation received through Christianity, and the mind begins to correct itself as you read.

Neither shalt thou make marriages with them: the Most High forbids marrying outside the nation. The seed of the fathers today is found among the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and Native Indians, who make up the twelve tribes of Israel; a spouse may come from any of the twelve tribes, but from within the tribes only. Going outside your nation for a husband or wife is despising your brethren in your heart. Whom you marry is the greatest commitment you make in this life; if you truly loved your people, you would choose one of your own people to become aged together with. They will turn away thy son from following me: the nations are strangers to the Most High and cannot come into this covenant, so they draw the Israelite spouse off to religions that accept everything. Christianity accepts that union, and that is how they turn you away from your God.
Thus shall ye deal with them: destroy their altars, break down their images, cut down their groves, and burn their graven images with fire. Nothing of their worship was to be spared or adopted.

For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: this is one of the most uplifting scriptures in the book, and it should be etched into your children's minds from the moment they begin to read, until it is implanted into their spirit. The mind controls the body: what goes into the mind comes out through the body, so a people that knows it is holy and special above all people walks and carries itself differently. Being chosen above all people keeps you out of the affairs of this world, their fashions, their hairstyles, their trends and challenges, and keeping up with the Joneses; you cannot flip-flop with every new wave and still carry the speciality the Most High put on you.

The Lord did not choose Israel for their number, for ye were the fewest of all people: only threescore and ten souls came out of the loins of Jacob when Israel first went down, as Genesis records, some places reading seventy and some counting seventy-five. But because the Lord loved you: the Most High needs no other reason, he simply loved us, and we should never apologize for that. He kept the oath sworn unto the fathers and redeemed Israel out of the house of bondmen, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt; Israel came out from under Rameses.

Know therefore that the Lord thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations, and repayeth them that hate him to their face. This is the same teaching as the new testament: loving the Most High is keeping his commandments, and refusing his commandments shows him with your actions that you hate him, and then judgment comes. From the jump it has always been the same: love God, keep the commandments; nothing changed between the covenants.

If ye hearken to these judgments and keep and do them, the Lord keeps the covenant and the mercy: he will love thee, bless thee, and multiply thee, blessing the fruit of thy womb, thy land, thy corn, wine, oil, kine, and sheep, blessed above all people, which goes right back to verse 6. The Lord will take away from thee all sickness and put none of the evil diseases of Egypt upon thee, but will lay them upon all them that hate thee. That still reigns true today: keep the commandments and the Most High will keep you from the diseases of modern-day Egypt, and if you do catch something, he will revive you and bring you back to your health.

Thou shalt consume all the people which the Lord thy God shall deliver thee; thine eye shall have no pity upon them, neither shalt thou serve their gods, for that will be a snare unto thee. Those days are coming back when Christ returns.

If thou shalt say in thine heart, these nations are more than I: fear them not, but remember what the Lord did unto Pharaoh and unto all Egypt, the signs, the wonders, the mighty hand and the stretched out arm; so shall he do unto all the people of whom thou art afraid. The Lord will send the hornet among them until even those that hide themselves are destroyed, and he will put out those nations before thee by little and little, lest the beasts of the field increase upon thee. He shall deliver their kings into thine hand, and thou shalt destroy their name from under heaven. There is no way to read [Deuteronomy 7](/bible/deuteronomy/7) and still say God loves everybody; that idea is being drunk on Christianity, not reading the book.

The graven images of their gods shall ye burn with fire: desire not the silver or gold that is on them, lest thou be snared therein, for it is an abomination to the Lord thy God. Neither shalt thou bring an abomination into thine house, lest thou be a cursed thing like it. Bring it up to today: the Jesus pieces, the crosses, the ankhs, and the rosary beads wrapped around the neck and rubbed in prayer make the wearer an abomination and a cursed thing just like the idol. The main abomination we bring into our house is the Christmas tree of Jeremiah 10: the tree cut down, fastened with nails and hammers, and decked with silver and with gold, whether cut from the forest or bought as a fake tree from the store.

lawsResolved.text: National punishment, captivity, curses and destruction for idolatry or worshiping false gods in the land.
Disobedience to God causes national captivity by heathen or enemy nations.
Backsliding from God's ways causes punishment and the loss of His protection.
We are not to intermarry with those who practice idolatry.
We are not to learn or follow the ways, customs or abominations of the heathen or of any ungodly nation.

text.text: And also all that generation were gathered unto their fathers: and there arose another generation after them, which knew not the Lord, nor yet the works which he had done for Israel.
And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and served Baalim:

And they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, which brought them out of the land of Egypt, and followed other gods, of the gods of the people that were round about them, and bowed themselves unto them, and provoked the Lord to anger.
And they forsook the Lord, and served Baal and Ashtaroth.

And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies.
Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn unto them: and they were greatly distressed.
Nevertheless the Lord raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them.

And yet they would not hearken unto their judges, but they went a whoring after other gods, and bowed themselves unto them: they turned quickly out of the way which their fathers walked in, obeying the commandments of the Lord; but they did not so.

And when the Lord raised them up judges, then the Lord was with the judge, and delivered them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge: for it repented the Lord because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them.

And it came to pass, when the judge was dead, that they returned, and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, in following other gods to serve them, and to bow down unto them; they ceased not from their own doings, nor from their stubborn way.
And the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, Hittites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Hivites, and Jebusites:
And they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods.
And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgat the Lord their God, and served Baalim and the groves.
Therefore the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Chushan–rishathaim king of Mesopotamia: and the children of Israel served Chushan–rishathaim eight years.
In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.
They did not destroy the nations, concerning whom the Lord commanded them:
But were mingled among the heathen, and learned their works.
And they served their idols: which were a snare unto them.
Yea, they sacrificed their sons and their daughters unto devils,
And shed innocent blood, even the blood of their sons and of their daughters, whom they sacrificed unto the idols of Canaan: and the land was polluted with blood.
Thus were they defiled with their own works, and went a whoring with their own inventions.
Therefore was the wrath of the Lord kindled against his people, insomuch that he abhorred his own inheritance.
And he gave them into the hand of the heathen; and they that hated them ruled over them.
Their enemies also oppressed them, and they were brought into subjection under their hand.
Many times did he deliver them; but they provoked him with their counsel, and were brought low for their iniquity.

Nevertheless they were disobedient, and rebelled against thee, and cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee, and they wrought great provocations.

Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them: and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven; and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.

But after they had rest, they did evil again before thee: therefore leftest thou them in the hand of their enemies, so that they had the dominion over them: yet when they returned, and cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven; and many times didst thou deliver them according to thy mercies;
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.
